inspiration: Water is a flat plane whose vertices are pushed up and down by a sine of their x plus z position, offset by a per-frame clock. A texture strip cycles through a fixed set of frames with a modulo index (src/Renderer/Map/Water.js lines 97, 232, 235). Recreate: a gentle ripple on a flat quad plus a looping caustic strip, our own palette, our own ripple direction.

Sky clouds are a fixed pool of about 150 billboards (src/Renderer/Effects/Sky.js line 30). Each cloud gets a random life, and its birth time is set 2 s in the past so the sky is already full when the zone loads (Sky.js lines 128 and 129). The pool-plus-random-life pattern costs no per-frame allocation.

The lock-on or cast ring is a flat disc that rotates each tick and changes brightness in 20 discrete steps over a 20-tick cycle, with a single tint uniform in the fragment shader (LockOnTarget.js lines 102, 157, 260). Discrete steps read clearly at 375 wide and cost almost nothing.

Damage numbers take their colour from the hit class and fade by the fraction of their life used (src/Renderer/Effects/Damage.js line 363). Keep colour-by-class and fade-by-life; change the rise path and the entry scale.

Sky colour and cloud tint live in one table keyed by map file name (src/DB/Effects/WeatherEffect.js lines 22 to 23). Each zone gets a sky and a cloud pair as data. Our zone data can carry the same two fields, extended to a gradient.

Blob shadow size is a small table keyed by monster ID, with a zero value for things that should have no shadow (src/DB/Monsters/ShadowTable.js, data structure read; numbers not recorded). Shadow scale as data, not code, is a clean catalogue-field pattern (row 21).

Catalogue IDs are kept apart from display text: numeric-keyed tables for items, monsters and skills, with text in the same keyed record (src/DB/DBManager.js loads them). Keep the ID and text split for our catalogue; write our own text.

The effect table resolves an effect name to a file name pattern, with a random number substituted for a placeholder (EffectTable.js header comment, read; no receipt). Idea: one effect name resolves to a random variant. Useful for blood and impact variety (row 8).

briefs.label: Ripple lake
briefs.why: A low-amplitude ripple reads as water at 375 wide without a heavy shader. Calm, cheap, and readable from a fight camera.
briefs.keep: Vertex sine driven by position and a time offset; a looping caustic strip with a frame index.
briefs.change: Recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy: ripples radiate from impact points instead of a global wave; our own palette; a green-grey tone instead of a blue pond; a different loop length.

briefs.label: Cloud pool drift
briefs.why: A fixed pool of sprites with random life gives a living sky and no per-frame allocation. Pre-aged spawns mean the sky never starts empty.
briefs.keep: Fixed pool, random life, back-dated spawn so the sky starts full.
briefs.change: Recreate as a clearly distinct original: fewer, larger shaped sprites in our palette; soft shadows drifting over the ground instead of clouds; spawn position tied to the zone wind direction.

briefs.label: Twenty-step lock ring
briefs.why: A rotating ground ring that pulses in discrete steps is a readable lock-on marker that reads at phone size.
briefs.keep: Flat rotating disc; discrete brightness steps; one tint uniform.
briefs.change: Recreate as a clearly distinct original: a segmented runic ring with two colours and a radial spoke; the pulse follows the target's threat level, not a fixed cycle.

briefs.label: Fading hit number
briefs.why: Colour by hit class plus fade by life gives an instant read of what happened in a busy fight.
briefs.keep: Colour set per hit class; alpha fades with life fraction.
briefs.change: Recreate as a clearly distinct original: a short punch-scale on spawn, an arc path, and our own glyph set; never the same font or rise path.

briefs.label: Zone sky pair table
briefs.why: One table of sky and cloud colour per zone makes each zone feel distinct for almost no code.
briefs.keep: A keyed table per zone with a sky colour and a cloud tint.
briefs.change: Recreate as a clearly distinct original: a three-stop gradient and a horizon band per zone, stored as zone data fields, not a map file name key.
